title: Graveyard Shift CV
premise: Each round, the Host announces a real but grimly ordinary job opening. You and your rival submit one line from a CV applying for it, then the Host crowns the applicant whose line wanders furthest from sensible self-preservation without losing the job’s required duty. Ceremonial applause for the desperate; medical concern for everyone else.

seed_pool.opening_token: Remove chewing gum from cinema seats after the final showing.
Clean the school toilets at midnight.
Count frozen chickens in a warehouse before dawn.

setting: a station after the last train

tests: One sentence, with an article and a clear duty. A stranger knows what the worker must do.
The job is legal, possible and grimly ordinary. Nobody is asked to commit a crime or face certain death.
The setting makes the shift unattractive without turning the card into a whole adventure.
It contains a duty and a setting a CV line can preserve while making the applicant look alarmingly willing.
It is short enough to remember and specific enough that a vague boast cannot fit every card.

move_constraints.example: I bring my own mop, a torch, and absolutely no questions.
move_constraints.hint: One CV line. Keep the duty and setting, then reveal why nobody else applied.

rubric.name: stretch
rubric.description: How far does the CV line depart from sane employment while still promising the named duty in its named setting?
rubric.anchors: 0 = merely repeats the job; 1 = adds one mild qualification; 2 = shows an odd habit, sacrifice or motive; 3 = reveals a troubling lifestyle built around the shift; 4 = turns the applicant into a magnificent professional disaster while the duty and setting remain intact, rare.

rubric.name: funny
rubric.description: Does the applicant’s dreadful enthusiasm, history or self knowledge produce a laugh?
rubric.anchors: 0 = no comic charge; 1 = a small twitch; 2 = a clear smile; 3 = a proper laugh; 4 = the line deserves to be read aloud at the ceremony, rare. A straight confession is usually funnier than a forced punchline.

rubric.name: headline_shaped
rubric.description: Does it work as one crisp CV line, with a claim or boast rather than an explanation?
rubric.anchors: 0 = not a CV line, a paragraph or a question; 1 = a claim buried under padding; 2 = recognisable but loose; 3 = concise, specific and employable at a glance; 4 = a recruiter could paste it into the application unchanged, rare.

criterion.description: A CV line PLAYS if it still shows that the applicant will perform the card’s named duty in the card’s named setting. It may add experience, motives, equipment, private rituals, terrible confidence or adult innuendo. It fails when the duty is dropped, the setting is changed, the applicant refuses the work, or the line makes the named task impossible. It also fails when it is not a CV line but a question to the Host, a comment on the game or an unrelated sentence. A sensible restatement plays and scores near zero on stretch.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Host, discussing the game or pleading for employment is itself a losing CV line.
judge_notes:
Test the gate first: could this applicant still perform the named duty in the named setting? For cleaning school toilets at midnight, I bring my own mop passes because both the cleaning and the midnight school setting survive.
A strange added detail is allowed. A torch, a sleeping bag, a criminal record or a suspicious emotional attachment may play if the named duty and setting remain possible.
Dropping the duty fails. A line about enjoying empty cinemas does not show that the applicant will remove chewing gum from seats.
Changing the setting fails. Cleaning the school toilets in daylight, or removing gum from a dentist’s chair, does not preserve the card.
Refusing or dodging the work fails. I will supervise from the car does not show that the applicant will clean the toilets.
Making the task impossible fails. I am allergic to cleaning products cannot preserve a cleaning duty unless the line still clearly promises a workable method.
Both players answer the same opening. Judge each line alone, never by comparing it with the rival’s line.
Score stretch by distance from sensible self preservation, not by the number of alarming adjectives. A quiet confession can beat a loud claim that says nothing.
Lower case, capitals, a missing full stop and ordinary spelling do not affect the gate or the score.

voice_rules: Use one sentence under 140 characters, or two short sentences at most.
Speak as though awarding a minor civic honour to a person who should perhaps be assessed by a doctor.
The reason must be clinical and exact. Name the duty and setting, then identify the applicant’s alarming extra commitment.
Never open with a status word or ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, or The Registrar declares.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, no ellipses. Commas and full stops only.
Roast the CV line, not protected identity. A jab at the applicant’s choices is permitted. Identity based abuse is forbidden.
Plain spoken English with ceremonial flavour. Do not bury a joke in grand fog or recruitment jargon.
On a fail, state which duty or setting vanished, changed or became impossible, using the card’s own words.
On a refusal, the line is refused and another is requested. It never rules on the rival or awards the round.
The coaching line must name one line that would pass. It ends on a duty or an action, never a mood or a verdict.
good_headlines: The gum is removed after closing, and courtship has been listed as a workplace hazard.
The school toilets receive their midnight attendant, along with a torch and an oath of silence.
The chickens are counted before dawn, while the applicant conducts a second inventory of their remaining years.
The mop is present, the hour is midnight, and the applicant has made secrecy sound like a qualification.
The cinema seats will be cleaned after the final showing, by a person apparently courting both gum and ruin.
The applicant still counts frozen chickens before dawn, which is more commitment than the chickens requested.
The duty survives. The setting survives. The applicant’s relationship with daylight does not.
A respectable CV would mention sanitation. This one mentions a torch, which is how the ceremony acquires witnesses.
The gum line keeps the seats and the late hour, then adds romance where no recruiter requested it.
The toilets will be cleaned at midnight, and the applicant has volunteered the final shred of common sense.

bad_headlines.why: opens with a status word and gives no clinical reason

bad_headlines.text: The Registrar refuses, kindly rewrite it.
bad_headlines.why: opens with a ruling phrase and names the host
praises without naming the duty, setting or joke
does not identify which named duty went missing

bad_headlines.text: Your line is stupid and you are hopeless.
bad_headlines.why: mocks the player rather than the application

bad_headlines.text: O midnight mop, arise and cleanse the moonlit throne.
bad_headlines.why: uses poetry instead of plain ceremonial speech

bad_headlines.text: The applicant demonstrates exceptional cross functional nocturnal sanitation synergies.
bad_headlines.why: uses padding and recruitment jargon instead of a clear image

bad_headlines.text: This wins because it is better than the other applicant.
bad_headlines.why: judges the pair rather than the line on its own

bad_headlines.text: A glorious, magnificent, unforgettable triumph of employability.
bad_headlines.why: uses several grand adjectives but gives no reason

bad_headlines.text: The toilets are cleaned, the moon is crowned, and destiny signs the form.
bad_headlines.why: becomes ornate fantasy and loses the plain clinical explanation

rules: Three rounds, one grimly ordinary job opening each.
Write one CV claim, boast or experience line under 90 characters. The House writes its own, unseen, and the Registrar scores both.
The line must still show that the applicant will perform the named duty in the named setting. Drop, move or sabotage either and the application is refused.
Everything else may be invented, including motives, equipment, habits, trauma and suspicious enthusiasm. Most points after three rounds wins.

labels.compose_waiting: Draft your application while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Blank application. Write the CV line.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 90 characters. This is a CV line, not a deposition.
validation_messages.duplicate: That line has already been filed this match. Find another reason to accept the misery.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. One line that keeps this true: {standing_form}.

judge_out_text: The Registrar has left to inspect the premises. Nobody is appointed until they return. {standing_form} remains under consideration. Give it a moment.
opponent_prompt:
You are applying for a job nobody wants, and your CV has one line to make the
Registrar fear your competence. Write one CV claim, boast, or experience line.
THE DUTY AND SETTING MUST SURVIVE. A reader who sees only your line must still know that
you will perform the named duty in the named setting. Never drop the work, never move
the shift, never make the task impossible.
Then go as far as you dare. Invent the applicant’s rituals, equipment, motives, history,
private bargains and appalling enthusiasm. The points are for distance from sensible
self preservation while the job remains doable.
Good: "I bring my own mop, a torch, and absolutely no questions." for cleaning school
toilets at midnight. "I have removed gum from seats for six hours and call it courtship."
for cinema seats after the final showing.
Bad: "I love empty cinemas" because it drops the gum removal. "I clean school toilets
in daylight" because it moves midnight. "I will supervise from the car" because it refuses
the duty.
Write one short CV line under 90 characters. Plain words, concrete details, no explanation.
A comma is fine. Do not use a colon or a dash. Capitals are fine but not required.
Vary the applicant’s damage from round to round: equipment, devotion, a grim history,
a private motive, a questionable skill. Never use the same shape twice in a match.
No quotation marks around the line. Reply with the CV line only.
default_move: I remain calm in places where sensible applicants resign
